title: Fatima, simply
hook: three children, a call to prayer, and the crowd's report of the sun in 1917

segments.voice: Yesterday, Lourdes: a spring dug from mud, the sick at the front of the line, and doctors who test every claimed cure. Your line was the waters. Who came to mind when you washed? Day one thousand three hundred forty-six.

Type the word Fatima into a search bar and stand back. Secrets. Prophecies. Countdown videos. Arguments about what was hidden and who hid it. Hours of it, all very dramatic. Underneath all that noise is a much quieter story: shepherd children in the hills of Portugal, a lady who asked them to pray, and a crowd that gathered in a muddy field and later told what they saw in the sky. The title of today's lesson has a second word in it, and it's the important one: simply. Today we set the secrets down and look at what the children were actually asked to do. Today's word is the village.
screen: `SECRETS, PROPHECIES, COUNTDOWNS.` → `UNDERNEATH, A QUIET STORY.` → `FATIMA, SIMPLY.`

segments.voice: First, the children. Lucia and her younger cousins, Francisco and Jacinta, were watching sheep near the village of Fatima when, by their account, a lady brighter than the sun appeared to them. She came back again over the following months. What she asked was not complicated. Pray the rosary every day. Pray for sinners. Turn back to God. The children took it seriously in a child's way: Francisco would slip off to pray alone, and Jacinta offered small sacrifices for others. Both are now honored as saints. Second, the sun. At the last of the visits, a large crowd came, in the rain. People there later said the sun seemed to spin and dance and plunge toward them, and that their soaked clothes were suddenly dry. Accounts differ, and some people present reported nothing unusual. The Church approved the apparitions, and, as we heard three days ago, no Catholic is required to believe them. Third, the message is old. Strip away the drama, and Fatima says what Jesus said when he first began to preach. In the Douay-Rheims of Mark's Gospel: "The time is accomplished, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the gospel." Repent is a call to turn around. Not a new teaching. The one Jesus opened with, repeated by children in a field. Fourth, the rosary. The lady's daily request wasn't a crusade or a secret code. It was beads in a pocket, prayer the size of a few minutes. That's Fatima, simply: pray, and turn around, and start again tomorrow.
screen: `CHILDREN ASKED TO PRAY.` · `THE SUN, AS THE CROWD TOLD IT.` · `AN OLD MESSAGE: TURN AROUND.` · `BEADS IN A POCKET.` · then, large: `REPENT, AND BELIEVE THE GOSPEL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray one decade. A decade of the rosary is one Our Father, ten Hail Marys, and a Glory Be. If you pray, you can say one now, slowly, using your fingers if you don't have beads. If you don't pray, count ten slow breaths on your fingers instead, and on each one, name one thing you'd like to turn away from, or turn toward. Either way, don't hurry. Ten is enough. When you reach the end, rest your hands. The bell holds the time.
Fatima. The Portuguese village where shepherd children said a lady asked for daily prayer and conversion, and where a crowd reported a sign in the sun. Today's word.
Your line: pray and repent. Today, pick one small habit to turn around from, and turn around once, even for an hour. Day one thousand three hundred forty-six.

howItsDone: Catholics who honor Our Lady of Fatima pray the rosary, often daily, as the children reported she asked; pilgrims visit the shrine at Fatima in Portugal, and her feast is kept in May.

fork.setup: you're one of the shepherd children. the lady asks you for one thing to do every day. what is it?
options: tell no one what you saw.
fork.reveal: by the children's account, she asked them to pray the rosary every day. Fatima, simply, is daily prayer and turning back to God.

trapdoor: what you thought: Fatima is about secrets and the end of the world.
what it means: shepherd children asked to pray daily and turn back to God, and a crowd that reported a sign in the sun.
what a scholar hears: an approved private revelation no one is required to believe, whose core message repeats Mark 1:15.

notes: Editor: fixed 'two days ago' to 'three days ago' (private revelation was day 1343); made 'repent means turn around' a gloss rather than a word-meaning claim.
No year is given in the voice; the index hook's '1917' and 'three children' are kept off the spoken text under the claims rule (the children are named instead). Confirm.
'Lucia and her younger cousins, Francisco and Jacinta': confirm (Francisco and Jacinta Marto were Lucia dos Santos's cousins, both younger).
Francisco slipping away to pray alone and Jacinta offering sacrifices for sinners come from Lucia's memoirs; paraphrased. Both were canonized; no date given.
The lady 'brighter than the sun', returning over following months, and the daily rosary request: paraphrased from Lucia's accounts; confirm.
The crowd's report (sun spinning, plunging; clothes suddenly dry) and that some present reported nothing unusual: confirm phrasing. Worded 'people there later said'.
'Repent means turn around' is a gloss on the Gospel's call to conversion, not an etymology claim; confirm acceptable.
howItsDone: 'her feast is kept in May' (13 May, optional memorial); confirm.
